Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
32-year-old female with acute left-sided headache with visual aura, nausea, and vomiting; clinical impression of first-episode migraine; symptomatic treatment advised and same-day review arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset severe left-sided headache started ~4 hrs ago.  
• Characteristics: Intensity 6/10; worse with movement; associated blurred vision with zig-zag lines, dizziness, and two episodes of vomiting; paracetamol taken 3 hrs ago with no relief.  
• Pertinent negatives: No limb weakness, gait disturbance, or prior similar headaches.  
• Past medical history: Previous kidney stones.  
• Family history: Mother with migraines and hypothyroidism.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) taken today; no regular medications.  
• Allergies: Denies known drug allergies.  
• Social / preventive: No pregnancy suspected; no other social history obtained.

Examination:  
No examination findings recorded.

Impression:
Likely first-episode migraine with aura.

Plan:
• Symptomatic treatment trial:  
  – Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Over-the-counter anti-sickness medication (name/dose not documented).  
  – Sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola) for hydration and symptomatic relief.  
• Arrange same-day in-person appointment for full neurological examination; patient may cancel if symptoms resolve.  
• Red-flag advice: Attend emergency department or contact clinic immediately if headache worsens, neurological deficits develop, or vomiting persists.  
• Follow-up: Telephone the practice to confirm improvement or attend scheduled review.

Quality checks:  
● Missing expected elements: vitals, physical examination, full medication/allergy reconciliation.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted (family history clarified as hypothyroidism).  
● Transcript quality acceptable; occasional connection issues but clinical details clear.
